optimizedCv.targetRoleTitle: Digital Product Manager, Developer Tools Platform
professionalSummary: Seasoned product manager with proven track record in steering the internal developer tools platform’s deployment service, driving automation, and enhancing release efficiency. Demonstrated ability to set strategic direction, prioritize backlog with cross‑functional stakeholders, and achieve measurable improvements in deployment success rates.
experienceHighlights:
Led direction setting for the deployment service, collaborating each sprint with platform engineering and rotating engineering teams to prioritize backlog. 
Chaired all eight deployment‑service release reviews, maintaining a comprehensive decision log. 
Increased automated, manual‑intervention‑free deployments from 62% to 84% within three months post‑rollback release, surpassing the documented baseline. 
Coordinated release alignment with platform engineering managers and consuming teams, ensuring clear decision ownership for dates and rollout order. 
Maintained up‑to‑date release notes, documenting limitations (e.g., automated rollback exclusions) and on‑call hand‑over details.
projectsAndWorkSamples: Year‑long monthly deployment report illustrating deployment success metrics, baseline, and rollback release impact, accompanied by the decision log for the rollback release (source: src_d8461019750d).
optimizedCv.evidenceBoundary: The provided resume excerpts and work sample confirm the candidate’s experience and achievements related to the Digital Product Manager role, but do not include independent third‑party validation beyond the internal platform reports and notes.

decisionBoundary.statement: Candidate’s evidence supports all role requirements; human review recommended to confirm fit.

role.roleTitle: Digital Product Manager, Developer Tools Platform

evidence.text: Set the direction for the deployment service on the internal developer tools platform; every sprint I settled the backlog order with platform engineering and a rotating group of the engineering teams that depend on the service.
evidence.notes: Direct statement of direction setting and backlog prioritization.

evidence.text: Chaired the review for all eight deployment-service releases that year and kept the decision log, including what was deferred and why.
evidence.notes: Explicit mention of chairing release reviews and maintaining decision log.

evidence.text: The share of deployments completed without manual intervention rose from 62 percent to 84 percent in the three months after the automated rollback release, per the platform's monthly deployment report against its documented baseline of 62 percent.
Lined each release up with the platform engineering manager and the consuming teams; dates and the order in which teams were moved over were the platform engineering manager's decisions.
evidence.notes: Shows coordination and record of decisions.

evidence.text: Kept the release notes current; they record, for instance, that automated rollback does not yet cover database migrations, and carry the hand-over notes the platform on-call rota relies on.
evidence.notes: Demonstrates maintenance of release notes and hand‑over documentation.

supportedClaims.claim: Candidate set direction and prioritized backlog for the deployment service.
supportedClaims.witness: Set the direction for the deployment service on the internal developer tools platform; every sprint I settled the backlog order with platform engineering and a rotating group of the engineering teams that depend on the service.

supportedClaims.claim: Candidate chaired all release reviews and maintained a decision log.
supportedClaims.witness: Chaired the review for all eight deployment-service releases that year and kept the decision log, including what was deferred and why.

supportedClaims.claim: Candidate increased automated deployments from 62% to 84% within three months.
supportedClaims.witness: The share of deployments completed without manual intervention rose from 62 percent to 84 percent in the three months after the automated rollback release, per the platform's monthly deployment report against its documented baseline of 62 percent.

supportedClaims.claim: Candidate coordinated release alignment with platform engineering and consuming teams.
supportedClaims.witness: Lined each release up with the platform engineering manager and the consuming teams; dates and the order in which teams were moved over were the platform engineering manager's decisions.

supportedClaims.claim: Candidate maintained up‑to‑date release notes and hand‑over documentation.
supportedClaims.witness: Kept the release notes current; they record, for instance, that automated rollback does not yet cover database migrations, and carry the hand-over notes the platform on-call rota relies on.

humanReviewChecklist: Verify that the candidate’s reported metrics align with independent platform data.
Confirm the candidate’s role in decision‑making for release dates and rollout order.
Assess the candidate’s experience with on‑call hand‑over processes.
